name: Optical/near-IR MKID array photon-counting readout (4-8 GHz frequency-multiplexed) with the array at 90 mK behind a cryostat window
plain_name: Count single photons of starlight with a superconducting detector array kept near 0.1 K
description: UVOIR microwave kinetic inductance detector arrays (PtSi resonators, 4-8 GHz feedline) are housed at 90 mK inside a dilution refrigerator (MEC uses an ADR at 90 mK), illuminated through the front-plate window by lasers at 405.9, 663.1 and 808.0 nm, and read out by the RFSoC-based MKIDGen3 system via a cryogenic HEMT/paramp signal chain; the readout must run stably for a full observing night (at least 8 h).
keywords: Count single photons of starlight with a superconducting detector array kept near 0.1 K

sources.citation: J. P. Smith, J. I. Bailey III, A. Cuda, N. Zobrist, B. A. Mazin et al., 'MKIDGen3: Energy-Resolving, Single-Photon-Counting MKID Readout on an RFSoC', arXiv:2406.09764 (2024)

reported_equipment: MKID Exoplanet Camera (MEC) adiabatic demagnetization refrigerator (90 mK)

requirements.rationale: Photons (lasers at 405.9-808 nm in the lab, the telescope beam at the observatory) reach the array through a cryostat window.
The microwave feedline carries the 4-8 GHz readout comb, so the coaxial wiring must pass at least 8 GHz.
The feedline input/output and the cryogenic amplifier chain require cold RF connections to the array.
Optional: observing requires continuous cold operation for a typical night of at least eight hours (a limitation for single-shot ADRs, not for continuous dilution refrigerators).

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
